chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Ismail ibn Jabir, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), regarding the worry/distress.

He (peace be upon him) said: 'You should perform ritual bath (ghusl) and pray two cycles of prayer, and say: O Reliever of the worry, and O Remover of the sadness, O Beneficent of the world and the Hereafter and Merciful to them both! Relieve my worry and remove my sadness. O Allah, the One, the Unique, the Eternal, who neither begot nor was begotten, and there was none equal to Him. Protect me and purify me and remove my affliction; and recite Ayat al-Kursi and the two Mu'awwidhat (Surahs 113 and 114).'

key_terms.الْمُعَوِّذَتَيْنِ: The two Surahs of protection (Al-Falaq and An-Nas)

ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed ritual and supplication for relieving anxiety and worry in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes a specific spiritual remedy for anxiety (hamm) that combines physical purification (ghusl) with devotional prayer (salat) and dhikr. The invocation emphasizes Allah’s attributes as the Reliever of distress and the Merciful to both worlds, reflecting the Shia emphasis on combining ritual purity with direct supplication to alleviate psychological burdens. This practice underscores the holistic approach in Shia tradition where spiritual remedies are integrated with tangible acts of worship to restore inner peace.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from one of his companions, from Ismail Bin Jabir, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> regarding the worries.

Heasws said: ‘You should wash and pray two Cycles of Salāt, and you should be saying, ‘O Reliever of the worries, and O Remover of the sadness, and O Beneficent of the world and the Hereafter and Merciful to them both! Relieve my worries and Remove my sadness. O Allahazwj, the Alone, the First, the Last who neither begets nor is begotten, and there does not happen to anyone as a match for Himazwj, Protect me and Clean me and Remove my afflictions’; and recite Ayat Al-Kursy [2:255] and Al-Muawwizatayn (Chapters 113 & 114)’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from certain individuals of his people from Isma’Il ibn Jabir from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“When you are concerned about something, take a shower and perform two Rak’at (a prayer consisting of two times bowing down on one’s knees) prayer and say, ‘O the One who clears up concerns, removes sorrow, O the Beneficent for this world and the next and the Merciful for both, change my concern to happiness, remove my sorrow, O Allah, the One and only Self- sufficient, who is not born from anyone nor has given birth to anyone, the like of whom there is no one, protect me, cleanse me and remove my misfortune,’ then read verse 255 of Chapter 2, Chapter 1 14 and 1 13 of the Holy Quran.”
